techniques.name: Jangly Arpeggiated Double-Stops & Open Strings
techniques.description: Brad Shepherd's signature opening riff, using 1st and 2nd string double stops while letting the open B and high E strings ring out with power-pop chime.

notes: Hold a partial E triad shape at the 9th and 7th frets
Strike with sharp, rhythmic downstrokes to cut cleanly through the mix
Allow the open high strings to drone continuously beneath fret-hand slides
Maintain crisp right-hand alternate picking when transitioning into the single-note fills
sequence: Slide into 9th fret G string (E note) and 9th fret B string (G# note)
Drop down to 7th fret double stops over the B chord change
Hit 6th and 5th fret double-stops over the A major chord
Resolve with a quick open string snap returning to the root E
tips: Keep fret-hand fingers curled to avoid brushing against ringing open strings
Use a bright bridge pickup setting with moderate gain to preserve string definition
Lock into the upbeat accents with the drummer's hi-hat pattern

techniques.name: Pumping Eighth-Note Palm Muting & Power Pop Drive
techniques.description: Tight, punchy rhythm guitar playing root-5th power chords with right-hand palm muting across the lower strings at 124 BPM.

notes: Rest the heel of the picking hand lightly across the bridge saddles
Execute consistent, tight downstrokes on eighth notes
Open up the mute slightly on the upbeat of beat 4 into each chord change
Switch cleanly between E5 (open), B5 (2nd fret A string), and A5 (open A string)
sequence: Chug 8 steady eighth notes on E5 with tight palm dampening
Shift to B5 on fret 2 of the A string, maintaining even pick dynamics
Shift down to open A5 for two beats
Pop back to B5 with an unmuted downstroke accent
tips: Do not press too hard with the palm or the notes will go sharp
Keep wrist loose and relaxed to avoid fatigue at 124 BPM
Emphasize the punchy kick-snare coordination in the band mix

sections.name: Jangly Open String Intro Hook
sections.description: The instantly recognizable Australian rock guitar hook, sparkling with ringing open strings and rhythmic double stops.
notes: Play high double stops on the G and B strings at the 9th fret
Let open high E ring out as a pedal point
Establishes the infectious, upbeat Australian power-pop groove

sections.name: Chugging Power Pop Verse
sections.description: Dave Faulkner's narrative vocals enter over tight, driving rhythm guitar chugging on eighth notes.
notes: Tight right-hand palm muting across the lower strings
Accents on beats 2 and 4 driving the groove forward
Open up the mute into the last beat of each phrase for a dynamic lift

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Dynamic Build
sections.description: Tension builds as the progression moves to C#m, alternating with A before a driving drum and guitar build on B.
sections.progression: C#m - A - C#m - A - B - B
notes: Barre chord C#m (4th fret A string) with full, ringing arpeggios
The shift to minor creates emotional vulnerability before the anthemic chorus
Crescendo on the B major chord building energy into the hook

sections.name: Explosive Singalong Chorus
sections.technique: Open Power Chord Strumming & Lead Licks
sections.description: The song explodes into the immortal Australian anthem chorus with roaring open chords and lead fills.
sections.progression: E - B - A - B - E - B - A - B
notes: Full unmuted power strumming with wide pick swings
Lead guitar doubles the vocal hook with tasty pentatonic fills
Ringing open strings give that quintessential 1980s Aussie pub-rock authority

sections.name: Brad Shepherd Melodic Lead Solo
sections.technique: Melodic Major Pentatonic Soloing & Scalar Walkup
sections.description: Brad Shepherd's energetic guitar solo, combining melodic pop hooks with gritty garage-rock bends and an ascending diatonic chord walkup.
sections.progression: A - E - A - E - F#m - G#m - A - B
notes: Solo starts over the IV chord (A major) giving it immediate freshness
E major pentatonic runs centered around the 9th and 12th frets
Scalar walkup (F#m -> G#m -> A -> B) escalates the pitch and excitement into the final chorus

sections.name: High-Energy Outro Jam & Final Chords
sections.description: Double choruses, energetic lead guitar commentary, and crisp staccato hits driving to an exuberant finish.
sections.progression: E - B - A - B (repeating) -> E (final hit)
notes: Ad-lib lead licks dancing around the repeating E - B - A - B progression
Band locks into staccato power accents on the final turnaround
Ends on a ringing, triumphant open E major chord

beginner.title: Open Chords & Steady 124 BPM Strumming
steps: Master the E, B, and A open and power chord grips
Practice transitioning cleanly between E and B without hesitation
Play through the verse groove using steady downstrokes at 100 BPM
Work up to recording tempo (124 BPM) with a metronome

intermediate.title: The Jangly Intro Riff & Pre-Chorus Build
steps: Learn the high double-stop shapes on the G and B strings for the intro hook
Coordinate the ringing open high E string pedal note
Master the C#m to A barre chord transitions in the pre-chorus
Work on palm muting control during the verses

advanced.title: The Brad Shepherd Solo & Full Live Performance
steps: Execute Brad Shepherd's melodic guitar solo with full dynamic bite
Play the ascending scalar chord walkup (F#m - G#m - A - B) cleanly
Combine vocal cadence cues with driving rhythm guitar
Replicate authentic Aussie pub-rock crunch and attitude

commonMistakes: Muting the ringing open strings in the intro riff by not arching the fretting fingers
Pushing the tempo too fast—124 BPM is a bouncy, driving groove, not a frantic thrash pace
Losing palm-mute consistency during the verse when transitioning between strings 6 and 5
Stumbling on the ascending scalar chord walkup (F#m -> G#m -> A -> B) before the solo climax
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Alternate picking warm-up across strings 1, 2, and 3
10 mins: Slow precision practice on the intro double-stop riff at 90 BPM
10 mins: Palm-muted rhythm endurance drills on E5, B5, and A5 at 124 BPM
15 mins: Practicing Brad Shepherd's solo and the ascending scalar walkup
10 mins: Full performance run-through with complete dynamic contrasts
focusAreas: Clean double-stop intonation and ringing open string pedal points
Palm muting dynamics between verses and roaring chorus strums
Quick position shifting during the pre-chorus and guitar solo
Locking into the tight snare backbeat with the rhythm section
metronomeWork: Practice intro riff at 100 BPM with click on all four beats
Increase to 124 BPM focusing on effortless right-hand stamina
Drill the ascending pre-solo walkup with quarter-note clicks to ensure rock-solid timing
